en.title: Counting Subsequences Whose MEX Lies in a Range
en.description: Given an array arr, count the subsequences whose MEX lies in the closed interval [l,r]. A subsequence is formed by choosing some positions of the original array, and the empty subsequence also counts; different choices of positions are counted separately even if their value sequences are identical. Output the answer modulo 1,000,000,007.
en.input: The first line contains n, l, r, and the second line contains n integers arr[i]. Original ranges: 1≤n≤3×10⁵, 0≤arr[i]≤10⁹, 0≤l≤r≤10⁹.
en.output: Output the number of position subsequences whose MEX lies in [l,r], modulo 1,000,000,007.
en.explanation: The original problem defines a subsequence as deleting elements at any positions while keeping the order, and explicitly states that the empty subsequence has MEX=0; the source solution's formula (2^c−1) also confirms that equal values at different positions are counted separately.
hints: If MEX=k, then each of 0..k−1 must be chosen at least once, no element with value k is chosen, and elements greater than k may be chosen freely.
